'''Darius Tiyon Miller''' (born March 21, 1990<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/milleda01.html|title=Darius Miller NBA & ABA Stats|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 17, 2013}}</ref>) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]] and finished his senior season by winning the [[2012 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]] on the [[2011–12 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|2011–12 Kentucky Wildcats]] team.

==High school career==
Miller attended Mason County High School, where he averaged 19.9 points, 7.9 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 2.9 steals per game and led the team to a state championship in 2008.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nbadraft.net/players/darius-miller|title=1 - Darius Miller | work=NBADraft.net|access-date=April 3, 2012}}</ref> After his senior season in high school, Miller was named the [[Kentucky High School Athletic Association|KHSAA]]'s men's basketball player of the year, commonly known as "[[Kentucky Mr. Basketball]]".

Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Miller was listed as the No. 8 small forward and the No. 42 player in the nation in 2008.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://rivals.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Darius-Miller-49898;_ylt=AnGAGrobuKmBoD4yYoPe9qnXO5B4|title=Rivals.com|website=Rivals.Yahoo.com|access-date=July 25, 2017}}</ref>

==College career==
Following Kentucky's 2012 national championship win, Miller was chosen to present a commemorative Kentucky jersey and championship ring to President [[Barack Obama]] during the team's visit to the White House on May 4, 2012. Miller is the only player from Kentucky to have been named Kentucky's "Mr. Basketball" (high school player of the year in the state), win a KHSAA state championship (Mason County High School) and claim an NCAA title with the [[University of Kentucky]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kentucky.com/2012/05/04/2175858/kentucky-basketball-teams-meeting.html|title=President Barack Obama honors Kentucky basketball champions|work=Kentucky.com|date=May 4, 2012|access-date=May 5, 2012}}</ref>

Miller finished his college career having played more games for the University of Kentucky than any other player.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bigbluehistory.net/bb/Statistics/careergamesplayed.html|title=Kentucky Career Leaders in Games Played|work=bigbluehistory.net|access-date=May 5, 2012}}</ref> The Wildcats' championship game and Miller's last collegiate match was his 152nd appearance for the team, surpassing [[Wayne Turner (basketball)|Wayne Turner]]'s previous record of 151 games. He and [[Deon Thompson]] of [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] are currently tied for sixth place in [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball career games played leaders|career games]] in NCAA Division I men's play, and have the most games among those who played in exactly four seasons.

==Professional career==
===New Orleans Hornets / Pelicans (2012–2014)===
Miller was selected with the 46th overall pick in the [[2012 NBA draft]] by the New Orleans Hornets. On August 22, 2012, he signed a multi-year deal with the Hornets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Darius-Miller/Summary/2364|title=Darius Miller Player Profile, New Orleans Pelicans, News, Rumors, NBA Stats, NCAA Stats, G League Stats, International Stats, Events Stats, Game Logs, Bests, Awards - RealGM|website=basketball.RealGM.com|access-date=July 25, 2017}}</ref> On December 31, 2012, Miller was assigned to the [[Iowa Wolves|Iowa Energy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-assign-darius-miller-d-leagues-iowa-energy|title=HORNETS ASSIGN DARIUS MILLER TO D-LEAGUE'S IOWA ENERGY|work=NBA.com|date=December 31, 2012|access-date=December 31, 2012}}</ref> On January 27, 2013, he was recalled by the Hornets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-recall-darius-miller|title=HORNETS RECALL DARIUS MILLER|work=NBA.com|date=January 27, 2013|access-date=January 27, 2013}}</ref> In April 2013, the Hornets were renamed the Pelicans.

On July 25, 2014, Miller re-signed with the Pelicans.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-re-sign-darius-miller-0|title=Pelicans Re-Sign Darius Miller - New Orleans Pelicans|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 25, 2017}}</ref> On November 30, 2014, he was waived by the Pelicans.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-waive-miller-and-young|title=Pelicans Waive Miller and Young - New Orleans Pelicans|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 25, 2017}}</ref>

On January 16, 2015, Miller was opted over another D-League player for a position on the Clippers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/marc-stein/post/_/id/3488/listening-in-from-santa-cruz-with-latest-buzz?ex_cid=espnapi_public|title=Listening in from Santa Cruz with latest|website=ESPN.go.com|date=January 16, 2015 |access-date=July 25, 2017}}</ref>

===Brose Bamberg (2015–2017)===
On February 24, 2015, Miller signed with [[Brose Bamberg]] of Germany for the rest of the 2014–15 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/153432/darius-miller-signed-with-brose-baskets-bamberg.html|title=Darius Miller signed with Brose Baskets Bamberg|website=Sportando.com|access-date=July 25, 2017}}</ref> On July 28, 2015, he re-signed with Brose Baskets for one more season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Brose Baskets completes roster with Miller|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/68e4bon5vp4erqty|access-date=July 28, 2015|work=Euroleague.net|date=July 28, 2015}}</ref> On June 7, 2016, he signed a two-year contract extension with Bamberg.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/201447/brose-baskets-bamberg-signs-darius-miller-to-a-two-year-contract-extension.html|title=Brose Baskets Bamberg signs Darius Miller to a two-year contract extension|website=Sportando.com|access-date=July 25, 2017}}</ref> On July 19, 2017, he parted ways with Bamberg in order to return to the NBA.<ref>{{Cite web | date=July 18, 2017 | url=http://www.brosebamberg.de/saison/news/artikel/news/detail/News/causeur-und-miller-verlassen-brose-bamberg/ | title=Causeur und Miller verlassen Brose Bamberg | trans-title=Causeur and Miller leave Brose Bamberg | language=de | website=BroseBamberg.de | access-date=July 25, 2017 | quote=Fabien Causeur und Darius Miller verlassen Brose Bamberg. Sie machen von ihrer im Vertrag verankerten Ausstiegsklausel Gebrauch, die gegen Leistung einer Ablösesumme umgesetzt werden kann. | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170731083610/http://www.brosebamberg.de/saison/news/artikel/news/detail/News/causeur-und-miller-verlassen-brose-bamberg | archive-date=July 31, 2017 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Return to the Pelicans (2017–2020)===
On July 27, 2017, Miller signed with the New Orleans Pelicans, returning to the franchise for a second stint.<ref>{{cite news|title=Pelicans Sign Darius Miller|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-darius-miller|access-date=July 27, 2017|work=NBA.com|date=July 27, 2017}}</ref> On November 13, 2017, he scored a career-high 21 points in a 106–105 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974946|title=Miller's late 3s rescue Pelicans in 106-105 win over Hawks|work=ESPN.com|date=November 13, 2017|access-date=November 13, 2017}}</ref>

On December 31, 2018, Miller scored 13 of his 21 points in the fourth quarter of the Pelicans' 123–114 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071222|title=Randle, Miller lead Pelicans past Wolves, 123-114|work=ESPN.com|date=December 31, 2018|access-date=January 1, 2019}}</ref> On January 24, 2019, he matched a career high<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071390|title=Westbrook's 15th triple-double leads Thunder past Pelicans|work=ESPN.com|date=January 24, 2019|access-date=January 24, 2019}}</ref> with 21 points in a 122–116 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].

On July 3, 2019, after becoming a free agent, he signed a two-year contract with the New Orleans Pelicans. On August 29, 2019, the Pelicans announced that Miller would be out indefinitely after undergoing surgery to repair a ruptured right Achilles tendon.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/darius-miller-medical-update-8-29-19|title=Darius Miller Medical Update|date=August 29, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=August 29, 2019}}</ref>

===Oklahoma City Thunder (2020–2021)===
On November 24, 2020, Miller was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/hill-cheatham-gray-miller-williams-201124|title=Thunder Acquires George Hill, Zylan Cheatham, Josh Gray, Darius Miller, Kenrich Williams, One First and Two Second-Round Draft Picks and a Trade Exception|work=NBA.com|date=November 24, 2020}}</ref> On April 8, 2021, he was waived by the Thunder after 18 appearances.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/miller-210408|title=Thunder Waives Darius Miller|work=NBA.com|date=April 8, 2021|accessdate=April 9, 2021}}</ref>

==National team career==
Miller represented the [[United States men's national basketball team|U-19 United States national team]] at the [[2009 FIBA Under-19 World Championship|2009 U-19 World Championship]] held in New Zealand, where they won the gold medal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/76843/sid/4034/tid/379/_/2009_FIBA_U19_World_Championship_for_Men/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150513010829/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/76843/sid/4034/tid/379/_/2009_FIBA_U19_World_Championship_for_Men/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 13, 2015|title=Darius Miller profile, FIBA U19 World Championship for Men 2009 - FIBA.COM|website=FIBA.com|access-date=July 25, 2017}}</ref>
